findings.title: Parent field points to the architecture document, not the slice plan
findings.description: The slice design's `parent:` frontmatter points to `project-documents/user/architecture/900-arch.maintenance-and-refactoring.md` (the architecture doc), while slice 911 (a sibling in the same slice plan) uses `project-documents/user/architecture/900-slices.maintenance-and-refactoring.md` (the slice plan). The review instructions explicitly tell me not to flag this, so this is informational only — flagging in case the convention is worth aligning across siblings later.

findings.title: Site-count accounting in the survey table is inconsistent with actual source
findings.description: Two rows in the "Confirmed sites" table disagree with what `grep -oE "'(complete|in-progress|not-started|deprecated)'"` actually returns from those files: (a) `statusNormalizer.ts` row claims "13 (of 16 total; 3 are alias keys, see Excluded)" but the map has 14 keys and 14 value-side literals (lines 5–18), not 16 — and there are no "alias keys" as a distinct category; every key is an alias. (b) `types.ts` row claims "5 (of 8 total; 4 are the STATUS definition itself)" but 8 − 4 = 4 sweep sites, not 5. Because the verification grep in Success Criteria is keyed to "zero matches in the six swept files," the counts themselves don't gate correctness — but the table is the developer's working map for verifying the sweep, and the post-sweep grep expects the developer to recognize "4 (STATUS const) + 3 (intentionally-excluded frontmatterSchema) + 4 (intentionally-excluded SliceStatus)" rather than the "5/8" figure cited in the survey. Recount both rows against the actual files and update the table; the rest of the design is sound.

findings.title: Architecture scope and principles alignment
findings.description: The slice directly addresses two of the architecture's explicit scope items ("Hard-coded values → configuration or constants" and "Pattern consolidation and code quality improvements") and complies with all three architectural principles: it is themed (one coherent sweep, not open-ended), it relies on the existing test suite as the regression guard (no behavior change without tests), and it has a clear "no remaining bare NormalizedStatus literals in production code outside types.ts" success criterion rather than an open-ended cleanup.

findings.title: Slice-plan entry alignment
findings.description: Slice plan entry #10 (`(910) Centralize NormalizedStatus Value References`, dependencies `[241]`, Risk: Medium, Effort: 3/5) matches this design precisely in description, dependency, scope files, and the "241 introduces the const; this slice completes the sweep of pre-existing sites" framing. No drift between the slice plan and the slice design.

findings.title: Exclusions are well-reasoned and bounded
findings.description: TD-2 (frontmatterSchema uses a different vocabulary — `not_started`, `deferred` with no `NormalizedStatus` equivalent) and TD-3 (`SliceStatus.status` is a workflow-position union, not `NormalizedStatus`) both exclude real correctness hazards, not just extra work. The `'unknown'` sentinel (ProjectModelBuilder line 181) is correctly excluded as an unrelated sentinel, and the ConsistencyChecker.ts file-size overage is correctly delegated to a separate, larger effort rather than being silently folded in.

findings.title: Proportionality
findings.description: No new abstractions, no helper functions, no new I/O paths, no new message types — purely a find-and-replace-with-verification sweep plus one widening type retype. The order-of-work section is appropriately granular for a 65-site mechanical sweep but does not introduce any heavyweight mechanism (no codemod tooling, no intermediate aliases) that would be overkill. The verification grep, before/after counts, type-safety spot-check, and behavior-unchanged test pass are exactly the right level for this kind of refactor.

findings.title: Failure modes and NFRs — not applicable to this slice
findings.description: This slice introduces no new I/O paths and no new message types — every code path it touches (file parse, frontmatter parse, task-file parse) already exists with its existing error-handling contract unchanged. The parent maintenance architecture states no NFRs, and the slice touches no I/O path that would inherit one from another architecture. No failure-mode enumeration or NFR restatement is required.
